chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eight are not permissible for marrying: your slave girl whose mother is your slave girl, or her sister is your slave girl; and your slave girl and she is your paternal aunt from breast-feeding; and your slave girl and she is your maternal aunt from breast-feeding; your slave girl and she is the one who breast-fed you; your slave girl and she had slept (with someone) until she is free with her menstruation; your slave girl and she is pregnant from someone else; your slave girl and she is upon an evaluation; your slave girl and for her is a husband.'

key_terms.الاسْتِبْرَاءُ: Purity period (waiting for menstruation to confirm non-pregnancy)

ai.seo_question: What are the eight conditions that make a slave girl prohibited for her master to marry according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details eight specific impediments to marrying one's own slave girl, reflecting the juristic nuances of the Umm al-Walad status in Shia fiqh. It distinguishes prohibitions rooted in permanent kinship (blood or milk) from those based on temporary states like pregnancy, nursing, or marital status, illustrating the interplay between manumission and marriageability. The enumeration serves as a practical legal guide for early Muslim communities regarding the rights and restrictions of female slaves within the household.
